brand_001:n1.prompt:
You are helping me generate a shortlist of brand-name candidates for a new company using {{vendor}}, our configured AI assistant. Before starting, ask me for any of the following that you don't already have: (1) a one- or two-sentence description of what the company does, (2) the industry or category, (3) target audience/customer, (4) any keywords, themes, or values I want reflected in the name, (5) tone/style preference (e.g., playful, technical, classic, invented word), (6) how many candidates I want (default to 20 if I don't specify), and (7) any names, words, or spellings to avoid.

Once you have these inputs, use {{vendor}}'s document creation and editing capabilities to produce a working document (exportable file) containing the candidate list. For each candidate name, include: the name itself, a one-line rationale tying it to my inputs, and a rough category tag (e.g., descriptive, invented, compound, metaphorical). Aim for a mix of styles unless I specify otherwise. Use {{vendor}}'s AI-generated insights to surface non-obvious but relevant word associations, wordplay, or naming patterns from my description and keywords.

Iterate with me: after the first draft, ask if I want more of a particular style, fewer of another, or different tone adjustments, and revise the document accordingly using {{vendor}}'s editing feature until I confirm the list is ready.

Do not check domain availability, social handles, or trademark conflicts in this step — that happens later. Your job here is only to generate and refine the candidate list.

When done, report back with: the total number of candidates produced, a summary of the naming styles/themes covered, and the exported document (or its location) containing the full list for my review.

brand_001:n2.prompt:
You are helping me evaluate brand-name candidates for my new company. Please ask me for: (1) the list of candidate names I want checked, (2) my preferred domain extensions (e.g., .com, .io, .co), (3) the social platforms I care about (e.g., Instagram, X/Twitter, TikTok, LinkedIn, YouTube), and (4) the country/jurisdiction whose trademark register matters most to me (e.g., USPTO for the US, EUIPO for the EU).

For each candidate name, do the following:
1. Domain availability: check the exact name plus close variants across my requested extensions using a WHOIS lookup or a domain registrar's availability search (e.g., via Namecheap or GoDaddy's public search page). Note which extensions are free vs. taken.
2. Social handle availability: visit each requested platform and check whether the exact handle (and one or two close variants) is available or already claimed. Note follower count/activity if the handle is taken, so I can gauge conflict severity.
3. Trademark conflicts: search the relevant trademark office's public database (e.g., USPTO TESS for the US, or the EUIPO database for the EU) for exact and close matches in relevant business categories. Also run a general web search for existing companies using the name to catch unregistered but active conflicts.

Compile a single table with columns: Name | Domain status (per extension) | Social handle status (per platform) | Trademark/usage conflict findings | Overall risk score (low/medium/high) with a one-line rationale.

Done looks like: every candidate has been checked across all three dimensions with sources noted, and the table is complete with an overall risk score for ranking. Report back the full table plus a short summary recommending the top 2-3 names with the fewest conflicts.

brand_001:n3.prompt:
You are helping me finalize the branding step for my startup by presenting a ranked list of candidate company names. Use {{vendor}} (my configured AI assistant) to do this.

First, ask me for: (1) the list of brand-name candidates already generated along with their scores/notes on domain availability, social handle availability, and trademark conflict risk — if I haven't provided this, ask me to paste it or point you to the file/document where it lives; (2) any weighting preference I have (e.g., domain availability matters more than social handles) — if I have none, use an even weighting across the three criteria; (3) how many top candidates I want shortlisted (default to 5 if I don't specify).

Once you have the inputs, use {{vendor}}'s document and code capabilities to: compute a composite score per candidate from the three criteria, rank all candidates from highest to lowest score, and produce a clean, exportable table (in a document or spreadsheet format) showing name, domain status, social handle status, trademark risk level, composite score, and rank. Where any scoring inputs look stale or incomplete, use {{vendor}}'s web-grounded search to double-check current domain/social/trademark status and cite the sources you used to confirm or update any entries.

Done looks like: a ranked, exportable document listing all candidates with their individual scores, composite score, and a short rationale note for the top-ranked options, plus citations for any freshly verified data.

Report back with: the finalized ranked list (top candidates highlighted), the file/document you produced and its location or export format, and any candidates where data was uncertain or conflicting so I can review them myself.
